findings.location: source.html — sentence mentioning original title of the hymn
findings.source_quote: It first appeared in his book The Passion of Jesus, and was originally given the title “The Song of the Seraphs.”
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the quoted original title into Afrikaans and preserve punctuation and emphasis tags. For example: replace “The Song of the Seraphs” with “Die Lied van die Sefare” (keeping the quotation marks). Do not change the surrounding HTML structure.
findings.translation_quote: Dit het eers in sy boek The Passion of Jesus verskyn, en is oorspronklik die titel “The Song of the Seraphs” gegee.

findings.source_quote:
Fruit of the mystic Rose as of that Rose the Stem:
The Root, whence mercy ever flows—the Babe of Bethlehem!
findings.suggested_fix:
Translate all substantive words into Afrikaans and correct mistranslations/leftover English. Preserve line breaks and tags. Example replacement (keeping stanza markup):
"Vrug van die mistieke Roos, en van daardie Roos die Stam:
Die Wortel, waaruit genade altyd vloei — die Kind van Betlehem!"
(Ensure 'Stam' not 'Stamm' and 'Kind van Betlehem' replaces the untranslated 'Baba van Betlehem'.)
findings.translation_quote:
Vrug van die mistieke Roos as van daardie Roos die Stamm:
Die Wortel, waaruit genade altyd vloei—the Baba van Betlehem!

findings.source_quote: Hark! how the heavenly anthems drowns all music but its own;
findings.suggested_fix:
Use an idiomatic Afrikaans rendering for 'anthems' and adjust grammar so the sentence reads naturally. Suggested replacement while preserving tags and line breaks:
"Hoor! hoe oorstem die hemelse loofwysies alle ander musiek;" or "Hoor! hoe oorstem die hemelse lofwysies alle musiek behalwe hulle eie;"
findings.translation_quote: Hoor! hoe oorstem die hemelse anthems alle musiek behalwe sy eie;

findings.location: source.html — sentence about mixing of stanzas
findings.source_quote: The 12 stanzas have been mixed and matched down through the years.
findings.suggested_fix: The translation uses 'gemeng en gemasjineer', which is incorrect/awkward. Replace with an idiomatic Afrikaans phrase preserving HTML, for example: "Die 12 strofes is deur die jare deurmekaar gebruik en saamgestel."
findings.translation_quote: Die 12 strofes is deur die jare gemeng en gemasjineer.

findings.location: source.html — Thring lyrics, stanza 3, untranslated word
findings.source_quote:
Who o’er a darkened world
In robes of glory infinite His fiery flag unfurled.
And bore it raised on high, in heaven—in earth—beneath,
To all the sign of victory o’er Satan, sin, and death.
findings.suggested_fix:
Translate all words including 'beneath' and render the stanza fully into natural Afrikaans. Preserve stanza line breaks and tags. Example replacement:
"Wie oor ’n donker wêreld
In gewade van oneindige heerlikheid Sy vurige vaandel ontplooi het.
En dit hoog gehou het, in die hemel — op aarde — benede,
Vir almal die teken van oorwinning oor Satan, sonde en die dood."
findings.translation_quote:
En dit hoog gehou het, in die hemel—in die aarde—beneath,
Vir almal die teken van oorwinning oor Satan, sonde, en die dood.

findings.location: source.html — Thring lyrics and other places: untranslated or partially-English fragments (multiple lines)
findings.source_quote: Who died, eternal life to bring and lives that death may die. / The Lamb once slain for them who bring their praises now, / Crown Him, ye martyred saints of old, the Lamb once slain for all;
findings.suggested_fix:
Several lines retain awkward structure or partial English sense in the translation. Render these couplets idiomatically and completely into Afrikaans while preserving stanza structure and punctuation. Example fixes:
- "The Lamb once slain for all;" => "Die Lam, eens geslaan vir almal;"
- "Who died, eternal life to bring and lives that death may die." => "Wat gesterf het om ewige lewe te bring en lewe wat die dood laat sterf."
